headline: Approved buying hunting signs and T-posts, pending parks director approval; recommended awarding three farmland leases to 3B Ranch.
summary: Two members of the public suggested separate hunting signs at entrances, the bridge, and the roundabout. The commission also agreed to revise the mowing schedule and prioritize trail maps. Skip row tillage is now allowed in town fields leased for vegetables and corn, and the cover crop date moved to November 15.
decisions: Approved buying hunting signs, T-posts, and installation materials, upon approval by the Parks and Recreation director; passed unanimously.
Recommended awarding the farmland lease bids for fields 4A&19A, 4C, and 8B to the highest bidder; passed unanimously.
Approved adding skip row tillage in town fields leased for vegetables and corn, and moving the cover crop date to November 15; passed unanimously.
Continued the transition project report to the December meeting.
Continued the property monitoring report for 205 Main St, Yalesville, to the next meeting.
Continued the property monitoring report for Marcus Cooke to the next meeting.

plain_text:
WALLINGFORD CONSERV ATION COMMISSION 
MINUTES OF REGULAR MEETING 
Room 3, Parks & Recreation Building 
6 Fairfield Boulevard, Wallingford, CT 
Thursday, November 12, 2026, 6:00 p.m. 
   
Meeting was called to order by Chairman Conor Makepeace at 6:06 pm.   
In attendance: Commissioners Erik Severson, Mike Miller, Jeff Borne, James Pyskaty, and Dianne Saunders; Environmental 
and Natural Resources Planner, (‘EP’) Sebastian Velez; two members of the public, Amy Anderson and Carol Borsari.   
Commissioner Jack Murphy joined the meeting at 6:13 pm. 
Not in attendance:  Commissioners Bruce Conroy and James Loughlin. 
   
1. APPROV AL OF MINUTES   
A. Regular Meeting, July 9, 2026 - hold 
B. Regular Meeting, August 13, 2026 - hold 
C. Regular Meeting, October 8, 2026 - hold 
   
2. TRANSITION PROJECT REPORT – J. Loughlin – continued to December meeting 
  
3. LIST OF TASKS IN PROCESS – feedback – full DRAFT list as typed by Cmmr. Saunders last month. The following 
were discussed as priorities: 
 
A. Mowing schedule 
• Cmmr. Saunders suggested adding revision of the proposed mowing schedule to the task list (Public Works’ 
mowing; vendor mowing when/what DPW cannot mow) – all agreed to revise proposed schedule 
• Discussed complaint by users about timing of mowing of butterfly meadow  – Commission understands timing is 
difficult for DPW.   
• Consensus to tie proposed mowing schedule into farmland lease field CMA mowing, due to eliminating CMA’s 
from leases. 
 
B. Trail maps:  consensus to prioritize this and get them in final form and on the town website (Park-Rec).  Need to add 
horse crossings to maps.   
Action step: Chair Makepeace to re- send mapping to-date and kmz info to EP Velez, Cmmr. Saunders to re-send 
horse crossing locations to EP Velez; EP Velez will adjust as needed, make the maps uniform in presentation, and 
send to Park-Rec Director in digital and pdf form for posting on the website. 
 
4. PROPERTY MANAGEMENT  
A. Trees of heaven (toh) – update on treatment:  Cmmr. Conroy not present (Marcus Cooke); TMP was worked on last 
month as reported; could not do further TMP toh’s, as weather window has passed  
B. 155 Grieb Rd – staff:  EP Velez reported on a leaf dumping complaint; he went out with staff from the Engineering 
Dept; town open space signs are intact; no evidence of dumping was observed during the field visit 
C. Proposal for memorial bench – follow-up – staff:  EP Velez spoke with Park and Recreation Director Kenny 
Michaels, who thinks it is a good idea;  Mr. Michaels prefers a wooden bench (less expensive).  Commissioners 
discussed town staff efforts in the past to have standardization of memorial benches, and a protocol for approval of 
same.  There maybe be something in the former EP’s files.  Cmmr. Borne requested CC see the Town protocol for 
memorial benches, if there is a formal one, at the next Conservation Commission meeting.  
Action step:  EP Velez will follow up to find out if there is a protocol for memorial benches and report back. 
 
D. Other – 2 members of the public discussed hunting signage.   
1.  They feel non-hunters are using the areas on hunting days but wearing regular clothing and are not aware of 
hunting.  They observed that most users do not stop to read the fine print on kiosk signs or entrance safety signs.  
They suggested the Town post a separate sign at entrances, the bridge, and the roundabout to inform people 
there is hunting. Discussion and recommendations by everyone present.
2.  Chairman Makepeace did a quick search online and found a simple, ready-made sign available for a reasonable 
cost.  He suggested mounting on metal T-posts during hunting season, then removing for the remainder of the 
year.  The more detailed hunting safety info at the kiosks would remain year-round. 
Motion:  Cmmr. Miller made a motion, seconded by Cmmr. Pyskaty, to purchase the bolder, simple 
hunting signs, T-posts, attachment hardware, and any additional installation materials needed, upon 
approval by Director of Park and Rec.  Motion passed unanimously.   
Action step:  E.P . Velez will send a letter to Park-Rec Director Kenny Michaels to inform him of this proposal. If 
Director  Michaels approves, the signs and related supplies could be ordered and installed by commissioners. 
  
5. PROPERTY MONITORING REPORTS – Report and hand in:  
A. 205 Main St, Yalesville – B. Conroy: continued to next meeting 
B. Marcus Cooke – E. Severson:  continued to next meeting 
C. Other -  reminder for next meeting: 
• 204 Main St Yalesville – B. Conroy 
• Marcus Cooke – E. Severson 
• Tyler Mill – J. Murphy/D. Saunders 
• Cooke Rd – D. Saunders 
 
6. FARMLAND LEASE PROPERTIES PROGRAM  
A. Bid status - Staff  
• E.P. Velez reported on the recent bid results for fields 4A&19A, 4C, and 8B; 2 bidders, no exceptions; highest 
bidder for all 3 was 3B Ranch 
• Cmmr, Saunders presented a DRAFT of the fields by lessee as background; several are due for re-bid; Cmmr. 
Miller commented on improvements made by the high bidder on other leases (no performance exceptions) 
Motion:  Cmmr. Murphy made a motion, seconded by Cmmr. Severson, for Conservation Commission to 
recommend awarding the bids for fields 4A&19A, 4C, and 8B to the highest bidder – passed unanimously 
 
B. Field specifications – recommendations for tillage specifications fields 1A & 1C 
• Cmmr. Saunders explained improvements in field conditions using deep zone tillage for vegetable and corn fields 
1A & 1C, and results of skip row tillage for vegetable and corn fields based on trials observed 
Motion:  Cmmr. Saunders made a motion, seconded by Cmmr. Miller, to add skip row tillage as allowable 
in town fields leased for vegetables and corn, and to move the cover crop date to November 15th for fields 
leased for vegetables and corn – passed unanimously 
  
7. REPORTS / CORRESPONDENCE   
A. Trails Work Group – TWG reps not in attendance; Chair Makepeace stated no report received   
B. Other - Staff – n/a 
  
8. EXECUTIVE SESSION pursuant to CGS §1-200(6)(D) discussion of the lease, sale, or purchase of real estate.  
Motion:  At 7:39 pm, Cmmr. Saunders made a motion, seconded by Cmmr, Borne, to enter into executive session.  
There were only commissioners and staff present for the executive session – unanimous  
Motion:  At 7:59 pm, Cmmr. Murphy made a motion, seconded by Cmmr. Severson, to come out of executive 
session – passed unanimously  
  
9. NEXT MEETING – December 10, 2026, 6 p.m.   
  
10. ADJOURNMENT  
Motion:  At 7:59 pm, Cmmr. Pyskaty made a motion to adjourn, seconded by Cmmr. Severson – passed  
unanimously 
 
Respectfully submitted by C. Makepeace, D. Saunders
